page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache distribution provides 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities include hardware support for AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions. Baseline network throughput is rated at 3 Gbps, and no local NVMe or SSD storage is bundled.

Benchmark results reveal steady single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-core scaling. The single-core score of 1558 in Geekbench and 1875.88 in stress-ng align with the median 50 percent bracket for its hardware class. Cryptographic throughput and compression tasks also demonstrate average capability, led by single-threaded gzip compression at 27.94 GB/sec and PassMark encryption scoring 3651.65. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput drops to the lower quartile, reflecting the limitation of its dual-core physical topology. Multi-threaded stress-ng scored 3870.22, while PassMark CPU achieved 5908.52. Memory bandwidth tests produced uncached read and write figures of 28.05 GB/sec and 23.62 GB/sec respectively, placing memory throughput in the lower tier.

The primary tradeoff for the ecs.g7t.xlarge centers on dense memory capability versus bounded compute scaling. It delivers stable baseline performance for workloads that depend on dedicated CPU access and instruction extensions like AVX-512 without requiring high parallel core counts. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers practical value for non-bursting, sustained general operations where standard memory density is required without paying for unused multi-socket compute. The hardware profile is appropriate for standard web serving, mid-tier application backends, staging environments, microservices, and moderate database or cache operations that operate within the 3 Gbps networking envelope.

It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a 3 Gbps baseline network throughput without bundled local storage. Instruction sets feature AVX-512 with VNNI alongside AES and SHA hardware cryptography. Benchmarks show reliable single-core compute performance and encryption execution situated in the middle tiers, while aggregate multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth reflect its two-core hardware ceiling. The instance represents a stable, non-burstable option for workloads requiring fixed CPU-to-memory ratios, including internal business applications, light-to-moderate web serving tiers, microservices, and general-purpose development or staging environments.
